items.followUp: Give two examples of simple communities.

rubric.why: Each example names a complex community.
rubric.description: First example of a complex community.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid example, such as a forest or pond community.

rubric.why: A second valid example completes the response.
rubric.description: Second example of a complex community.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid example.

modelAnswer: A forest is a complex community.
A pond is another example of a complex community.

items.followUp: How has the study of living things benefited humans since ancient times?

rubric.why: The statement refers to humans observing or studying organisms throughout history.
rubric.description: Explains that humans have long observed or studied living things.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning human observation or study of organisms.

rubric.why: Examples show how knowledge of organisms has served human needs.
rubric.description: Gives a purpose or benefit of this study.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example, such as obtaining food or medicines, or domesticating animals.

modelAnswer: Since ancient times, humans have observed and studied the living things around them.
They have learned to use plants and animals for food, medicines, and other needs.

items.followUp: What is meant by induction in biological reasoning?

rubric.description: States that deduction leads to a specific or particular conclusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the conclusion as specific or particular.

rubric.why: Deduction applies a general principle to reach a particular conclusion.
rubric.description: States that the conclusion is drawn from a general principle or statement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the starting point as general.

modelAnswer: Deduction is reasoning from a general principle or statement to a specific conclusion.

items.followUp: What is the importance of saliva in a leech?

rubric.why: Mosquito saliva contains an anticoagulant that keeps blood from clotting while it feeds.
rubric.description: Identifies the anti-clotting action of mosquito saliva.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it prevents blood clotting or acts as an anticoagulant.

rubric.why: Preventing clotting helps the mosquito take in blood.
rubric.description: Explains how this helps the mosquito feed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the saliva's action to blood feeding.

modelAnswer: Mosquito saliva contains an anticoagulant that prevents the blood from clotting.
This allows the mosquito to suck blood while feeding.

items.followUp: Draw and label a plant cell.

rubric.why: These labels identify the mitochondrion's membranes and the folds of its inner membrane.
rubric.description: Labels the outer and inner membranes or cristae.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly labelling the outer membrane and inner membrane/cristae.

rubric.why: The matrix and intermembrane space are key internal regions of a mitochondrion.
rubric.description: Labels an internal region of the mitochondrion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly labelling the matrix or intermembrane space.

modelAnswer: Draw an oval mitochondrion with a double boundary; show the inner membrane folded inward to form cristae.
Label the outer membrane, inner membrane, cristae, and matrix.

items.followUp: Give two differences between skeletal and cardiac muscles.

rubric.why: Voluntary muscles are controlled consciously, whereas involuntary muscles are not.
rubric.description: Compares control of the two muscle types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting voluntary and involuntary control.

rubric.why: The two types differ in their usual location.
rubric.description: Compares their location in the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that voluntary muscles are typically attached to bones and involuntary muscles occur in internal organs.

modelAnswer: Voluntary muscles work under conscious control; involuntary muscles work without conscious control.
Voluntary muscles are usually attached to bones, whereas involuntary muscles are found in the walls of internal organs.

items.followUp: State two differences between fungi and plants.

rubric.why: Unlike plants, fungi do not have chlorophyll and obtain food heterotrophically.
rubric.description: Gives a nutritional difference between fungi and plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fungi lack chlorophyll or are heterotrophic.

rubric.why: Fungal cell walls contain chitin, while plant cell walls contain cellulose.
rubric.description: Gives a cell-wall difference between fungi and plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting chitin in fungi with cellulose in plants.

modelAnswer: Fungi lack chlorophyll and are heterotrophic, whereas plants generally make food by photosynthesis.
Fungal cell walls contain chitin, while plant cell walls contain cellulose.

items.followUp: Explain one way habitat destruction can reduce biodiversity.

rubric.why: Overhunting reduces the numbers of hunted organisms and can cause extinction.
rubric.description: Explains the effect on hunted populations or species.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that populations decline or species may become extinct.

rubric.why: Loss of species can disrupt ecological relationships and reduce biodiversity.
rubric.description: Explains the wider effect on biodiversity or ecosystem balance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking overhunting to reduced biodiversity or disrupted food chains/ecological balance.

modelAnswer: Overhunting reduces the populations of hunted species and may drive them to extinction.
This reduces biodiversity and can disrupt food chains and the ecological balance.
